claims.head: Hofer’s rough record against the Sharks is a coincidence
claims.body: Since 2023-24, Hofer has been shaky against the Sharks, well below his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Expect the usual Hofer.
claims.nums: 6 starts against San Jose: .877 save percentage · .914 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Hofer’s record against the Sharks.
claims.call: If Hofer starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .914 than to his .877 against the Sharks.
claims.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against San Jose, 2,689 shots against everyone else

check.rule: held if he starts and his save percentage is closer to his usual than to his record against this team; can't judge if he doesn't start

claims.head: The Blues should get some good looks
claims.call: The Blues’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
claims.body: The Blues make their shots count, and the Sharks are near the bottom of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Blues to get some real chances.
claims.nums: St. Louis 6th for shot quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · San Jose 23rd for preventing dangerous shots
claims.gist: The Blues make their shots count, and the Sharks allow dangerous ones.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season

check.measure: the average shot’s chance of going in, by expected goals
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Don’t blink and you still might miss the shots
claims.call: The game runs at fewer than 78.4 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, slower than either team’s usual.
claims.body: San Jose plays some of the league’s slowest games, and so does St. Louis. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.
claims.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): San Jose 29th (78.4), St. Louis 28th (78.5)
claims.gist: Both teams play slow, low-event hockey.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season

check.measure: shots per 60 at 5-on-5 (blocked shots left out), both teams combined, adjusted for score and venue
check.rule: held if tonight's pace is below the slower team's usual; partly if below the league average; otherwise didn't happen

STL.head: St. Louis should have the upper hand
STL.body: St. Louis has had more of the chances over recent games and has home ice. San Jose can make it interesting if their penalty kill holds up.

SJS.head: Not an easy night for San Jose
SJS.body: St. Louis has had more of the chances over recent games and has home ice. San Jose can pull it off if their penalty kill holds up.

story.head: Round two in St. Louis
paras: The Sharks already came to St. Louis once this season and left with a 3-2 overtime win. The Blues haven’t won in three. The Sharks are 3-1-0.
Don’t read much into Hofer’s record against the Sharks. The Blues make their shots count, and the Sharks allow dangerous ones.
